libraries.title: SDCAlertView
libraries.author: sberrevoets
libraries.summary: SDCAlertView started out as an alert that looked identical to UIAlertView, but had support for a custom content view. With the introduction of UIAlertController in iOS 8, the project was updated to the more modern API that UIAlertController brought.

verified.via: MotionBook app 3.6 live demo (built, run and screenshot-reviewed)

libraries.usage:
let alert = AlertController(title: "SDCAlertView", message: "Looks like UIAlertController, behaves like your own view.", preferredStyle: .alert)
alert.addAction(AlertAction(title: "Cancel", style: .normal))
alert.addAction(AlertAction(title: "OK", style: .preferred))
alert.present()

let alert = AlertController(title: "Working", message: "Custom content view with a spinner…")
alert.contentView.addSubview(spinner)
NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
    spinner.centerXAnchor.constraint(equalTo: alert.contentView.centerXAnchor),
    spinner.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: alert.contentView.topAnchor),
    spinner.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: alert.contentView.bottomAnchor),
])
alert.addAction(AlertAction(title: "Stop", style: .preferred))
alert.present()

let alert = AlertController(title: "Dismissal rules", message: "Only the preferred action closes this alert.")
alert.addAction(AlertAction(title: "Doesn't dismiss", style: .normal))
alert.addAction(AlertAction(title: "Dismiss", style: .preferred))
alert.shouldDismissHandler = { $0?.title == "Dismiss" }
alert.present()

libraries.title: YNDropDownMenu
libraries.author: younatics
libraries.summary: ✨The eligible dropdown menu, written in Swift 3, appears dropdown menu to display a view of related items when a user click on the dropdown menu. You can customize dropdown view whatever you like (e.g. UITableView, UICollectionView... etc)

verified.via: MotionBook app 3.6 live demo (built, run and screenshot-reviewed)

libraries.usage:
let view = YNDropDownMenu(frame: CGRect(x: 0, y: 64, width: UIScreen.main.bounds.size.width, height: 38), dropDownViews: _ZBdropDownViews, dropDownViewTitles: ["Apple", "Banana", "Kiwi", "Pear"])

view.setStatesImages(
    normalImages: Array(repeating: UIImage(named: "arrow_nor", in: .module, compatibleWith: nil), count: menuCount),
    selectedImages: Array(repeating: UIImage(named: "arrow_sel", in: .module, compatibleWith: nil), count: menuCount),
    disabledImages: Array(repeating: UIImage(named: "arrow_dim", in: .module, compatibleWith: nil), count: menuCount)
)
view.setLabelColorWhen(normal: UIColor.black, selected: FFA409, disabled: UIColor.gray)
view.setLabelFontWhen(normal: UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 12), selected: UIFont.boldSystemFont(ofSize: 12), disabled: UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 12))

view.backgroundBlurEnabled = true

view.alwaysSelected(at: 0)

self.view.addSubview(view)
